method_note: Consolidated from 71 candidate gaps proposed by segment agents S01-S14 (S00 is an architecture overview with no candidates). Merges are by shared workflow/mechanism, not by segment. evidence_forms counts DISTINCT evidence forms with at least one FACT-labelled pointer among: government document; exercise/operator workaround; RFI/Sources Sought/SBIR topic; budget line; product failure vs requirement; multiple partial-solution startups without scale; repeated procurement; documented manual workaround. Company claims and RECALL items are cited but not counted. IDIQ/OTA ceilings cited are ceilings, not revenue; prototype awards are not deployments. No fresh web searches were run this session (all pointers come from the prior evidence base); items not re-verified are labelled. Entries are ordered roughly by initial attractiveness; G20-G28 are deliberately weak or J-rated so the red team can kill them explicitly.

gaps.title: Machine-readable security labeling and releasability at the point of production (born-releasable C2/ISR objects: tracks, reports, video, AI detections)
gaps.problem: Tracks, reports, video and AI-derived products are created on U.S. Secret systems without interoperable, machine-enforceable classification/releasability tags (ACP-240/ZTDF/IC-TDF), so ABAC and cross-domain filters cannot decide automatically and staff regenerate, re-key or hand-carry products to partner enclaves after weeks of phone-and-email negotiation.
gaps.user: Intelligence and fires staff producing REL products (35F/35G analysts, targeting officers), foreign disclosure officers, multinational intelligence cell analysts, CDS filter engineers, NGC2/data-layer integrators

key_evidence_pointers.note: FACT/HIGH (2025-04-08): GAO finds overly restrictive, system-level classification a 'significant hindrance' to sharing C2 data with allies and no DoD entity owns the fix (government document).

FACT/HIGH (MIPB 2025, WFX 24-03): intelligence produced at collateral Secret could not be shared and had to be regenerated on the MPE enclave with REL NATO markings using a different tool (documented manual workaround / exercise).

FACT/MEDIUM (DoD CIO ZT PfMO webinar, 2025-09-18): tagging coordination today is 'phone calls, IERs, weeks of negotiation' with incompatible local definitions; ZTDF/ABAC named as the target (government document; mirrored transcript).
FACT/HIGH (2026-05): first eight-nation COP at Balikatan 2026 took 'more than eight years' of integration and still depends on JICOs and foreign-disclosure officers (exercise).
FACT/MEDIUM (FY27 Joint Staff J6 justification): ACP-240, ICAM and Zero Trust listed as coalition 'testing standards' for Bold Quest-type events (budget line; exact PE not extracted).
FACT/HIGH (2025, primary page blocked in-session): DEVCOM C5ISR RFI for Zero Trust Data Pillar protection of tactical data-in-use in DDIL, which presupposes machine-readable labels (RFI).
FACT/MEDIUM (2024-11-18): INDOPACOM partner data still moved by thumb drives/CDs and attachments blocked for lack of data-sharing policy (documented manual workaround).

gaps.notes: Chain steps: NORMALIZE, STORE, DISSEMINATE; echelons: division/corps, theater/joint, coalition. Multiple partial-solution vendors exist (Virtru, Anchor, Fortra) but none is fielded as the tactical object-level labeling service (INFERENCE, MEDIUM). Killer risks carried from segments: disclosure authorities may never accept machine-generated release decisions; marking policy is human-in-the-loop by regulation; a non-U.S.-person founder cannot legally work with classified marking guides or CUI export-controlled data - needs counsel, not a founder judgement. S04-G5 (releasability-aware dissemination of AI intelligence) merged as a sub-scope; the segment rated it J for this team. Entry vehicles: Joint Staff J6/Bold Quest, Army xTech, DoD CIO/DISA SBIR (ownership test applies), NATO DIANA.
